note: 120 unreviewed candidates for the pinned historical 40-section corpus: 40 factual (including four API-parameter questions), 25 troubleshooting/paraphrase, 20 multi-section, 15 comparison and 20 unsupported. The original core-001 through core-020 objects and their source spans are copied unchanged from the preserved v1 dataset. The original 20 remain development-exposed; all 100 additions have candidate splits and cannot be evaluated before assignment. This is not a 60/60 freeze. The 100 additions have not been run through retrieval, generation or judging. Known development-exposed questions/groups must stay out of held-out data. Group IDs and positive-only grades are provisional, not exhaustive judgments or proof of independence. Human review of scope, answers, qualifiers, alternative evidence, groups and split is required before freezing/scoring a new dataset. Historical source statements do not verify current AWS behavior.

questions.query: One part of my multipart upload failed in transit. Do I need to restart the whole object upload?
questions.reference_answer: No. Retransmit the failed part; this does not affect other uploaded parts. S3 assembles the object after all parts are uploaded.

questions.query: What happens if I upload a new multipart part using a part number I already uploaded?
questions.reference_answer: The new part overwrites the previously uploaded part with that part number.

questions.query: Can I assume that the ETag returned after completing a multipart upload is the MD5 hash of the object?
questions.reference_answer: No. The combined object ETag is not necessarily an MD5 hash of the object data.

questions.query: ListParts has more than 1,000 uploaded parts to return. Which response fields and next request parameter let me fetch the rest?
questions.reference_answer: A response returns at most 1,000 parts. If IsTruncated is true, use its NextPartNumberMarker value as the part-number-marker query parameter in the next ListParts request.

questions.query: I aborted a multipart upload while parts were still uploading. How can I check that all part storage has been freed?
questions.reference_answer: In-progress part uploads may still succeed or fail, so aborting the upload more than once may be necessary. Call ListParts and verify that its parts list is empty.

questions.query: Does an HTTP 200 OK header from CompleteMultipartUpload always mean the upload completed successfully?
questions.reference_answer: No. Processing can fail after the initial 200 OK header, and an error can be embedded in that response. A direct API client must parse the response body and handle the result.

questions.query: Can a single S3 GET retrieve two disjoint byte ranges from one object?
questions.reference_answer: No. The selected guide says S3 does not support retrieving multiple ranges of data in one GET request.

questions.query: What happens if the checksum I send with an upload differs from the checksum S3 calculates using that algorithm?
questions.reference_answer: S3 compares the supplied checksum with its calculated value and reports an error if they do not match.

questions.query: Can I use PutObject to change just one metadata value without sending the entire object?
questions.reference_answer: No. PutObject cannot update only a single metadata value; put the entire object with the updated metadata.

questions.query: For a missing object, why might HeadObject return 403 rather than 404?
questions.reference_answer: For a missing object, S3 returns 404 when the requester has s3:ListBucket on the bucket and 403 when that permission is absent.

questions.query: Will a bucket policy denying every action stop an existing S3 Lifecycle rule from deleting or transitioning objects?
questions.reference_answer: No. A bucket policy cannot prevent deletions or transitions performed by an S3 Lifecycle rule; the lifecycle configuration still functions normally.

questions.query: If a bucket has less restrictive Block Public Access settings than its account, which settings does S3 apply?
questions.reference_answer: S3 applies the most restrictive combination of the applicable access point, bucket, and account Block Public Access settings.

questions.query: Does changing an existing object’s tags create a new version in a versioning-enabled bucket?
questions.reference_answer: No. Changing tags does not PUT a new object, so it does not create a new object version. Operations such as CopyObject can create versions because they implement a PUT.

questions.query: How does GET respond when the current version is a delete marker, compared with a GET explicitly requesting the delete marker’s version ID?
questions.reference_answer: Without versionId and with a current delete marker, S3 returns 404 and x-amz-delete-marker: true. When versionId identifies a delete marker, S3 returns 405, that header, and Last-Modified for GetObject or HeadObject.

questions.query: The current version is a delete marker. Will deleting by key alone remove that marker, and how do I remove the marker permanently?
questions.reference_answer: A key-only DeleteObject adds another delete marker. To remove the delete marker permanently, specify that marker’s version ID in DeleteObject.

questions.query: Does an ordinary lifecycle Expiration action remove noncurrent versions, or is a separate action needed?
questions.reference_answer: Ordinary object expiration affects only the current version. Use NoncurrentVersionExpiration to permanently delete noncurrent versions; those deleted versions cannot be recovered.

questions.query: Can I apply an AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload lifecycle action using a tag-based filter?
questions.reference_answer: No. A lifecycle rule using AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload cannot specify a tag-based filter.

questions.query: What information should my uploader retain for CompleteMultipartUpload, and should I build that request from the returned multipart listing?
questions.reference_answer: Retain each uploaded part number and the ETag S3 returns and include them in completion. Maintain your own list: the guide says to use returned listings only for verification, not to construct the completion request.

questions.query: Is my production bucket customer-invoices public right now?
questions.reference_answer: The selected documentation cannot establish the live access state of a particular bucket.
questions.unanswerable_reason: The corpus contains documentation, not live account or bucket policy/configuration state.

questions.query: How do I configure CreateSession authentication for an S3 Express One Zone directory bucket?
questions.reference_answer: The selected general-purpose-bucket corpus does not include the directory-bucket session procedure.
questions.unanswerable_reason: S3 Express and directory-bucket operational procedures are explicitly outside the selected corpus.

questions.query: In the selected upload snapshot, what is the largest file the S3 console can upload, and which interfaces are suggested above that limit?
questions.reference_answer: The snapshot gives a 160 GB console limit. For larger files it names the AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, or S3 REST API.

questions.query: What single-PUT object-size ceiling is stated in the selected upload overview?
questions.reference_answer: The selected historical overview says a single PUT operation can upload an object up to 5 GB.

questions.query: At about what object size does the selected guide suggest considering multipart upload?
questions.reference_answer: It recommends considering multipart upload when the object size reaches 100 MB.

questions.query: What identifier does CreateMultipartUpload return, and how does its selected API description say subsequent part and final requests use it?
questions.reference_answer: It returns an upload ID associating the parts of that upload. Include it in upload-part requests and the final complete or abort request.

questions.query: What part-number range does the selected guide allow, and what does a part number identify?
questions.reference_answer: Part numbers range from 1 through 10,000. A number identifies a part and its position in the object.

questions.query: When a multipart upload completes, what determines the order in which S3 concatenates its parts?
questions.reference_answer: S3 concatenates the parts in ascending order of part number.

questions.query: What happens to object metadata supplied at multipart initiation when the upload is successfully completed?
questions.reference_answer: S3 associates that metadata with the assembled object. The separate uploaded parts no longer exist after successful completion.

questions.query: Does the selected multipart overview assign an automatic expiry time to an initiated upload?
questions.reference_answer: No. It says there is no expiry after initiation; the upload must explicitly be completed or stopped.

questions.query: In the ListParts description, what is the default maximum number of parts returned, and which parameter can reduce a response's part count?
questions.reference_answer: The default and maximum are 1,000 parts. The max-parts request parameter can restrict the number returned.

questions.query: Which four SHA or CRC checksum algorithms are listed in the selected object-integrity passage?
questions.reference_answer: CRC-32, CRC-32C, SHA-1, and SHA-256.

questions.query: How does the selected integrity guide say to apply an additional checksum algorithm to data already uploaded to S3?
questions.reference_answer: Copy the object. During copying, choose whether to retain its checksum algorithm or use a new one.

questions.query: After an upload, what must be consistent between a retrieved checksum and the local checksum used to verify it?
questions.reference_answer: Compare the retrieved value with a precalculated or previously stored checksum computed using the same algorithm.

questions.query: What prerequisite does the selected download guide state for downloading an archived object?
questions.reference_answer: An archived object must be restored before downloading it. Nonarchived objects are accessible in real time.

questions.query: What access route does the selected download guide suggest when I need an object I do not own?
questions.reference_answer: Ask the object owner to generate a presigned URL that allows the download.

questions.query: Can S3 Block Public Access settings be configured separately on one object according to the selected guide?
questions.reference_answer: No. The supported levels are access points, buckets, and AWS accounts, not individual objects.

questions.query: What geographic scope and propagation caveat apply to account-level Block Public Access settings in the selected guide?
questions.reference_answer: They apply globally across AWS Regions. They may not take effect everywhere immediately or simultaneously, but eventually propagate to all Regions.

questions.query: With BlockPublicAcls enabled, how does S3 treat a PUT Object request that includes a public ACL?
questions.reference_answer: The request fails. The setting rejects the specified operations when they include a public ACL; it does not modify existing policies or ACLs.

questions.query: Does enabling IgnorePublicAcls delete the public ACLs already stored on a bucket and its objects?
questions.reference_answer: No. S3 ignores the public ACLs for access enforcement, but the setting does not change their persistence or prevent new public ACLs from being set.

questions.query: Who can associate a bucket policy with a bucket, and what kind of policy is it?
questions.reference_answer: Only the bucket owner can associate it. It is a resource-based policy for the bucket and its objects; the selected generic description limits the attached permissions to objects owned by the bucket owner.

questions.query: With Object Ownership set to Bucket owner enforced, who owns uploaded objects and which access mechanism replaces ACLs?
questions.reference_answer: The bucket owner owns all objects. ACLs are disabled and access is managed exclusively using policies.

questions.query: Can an application choose or edit an S3 version ID, and how does the selected passage describe its format?
questions.reference_answer: Only S3 generates version IDs and they cannot be edited. They are opaque, URL-ready, UTF-8-encoded Unicode strings no longer than 1,024 bytes.

questions.query: When versioning is enabled on an existing bucket, are the IDs, contents, or permissions of its existing objects rewritten?
questions.reference_answer: No. Existing objects retain their null version IDs, contents, and permissions. Objects subsequently added receive version IDs.

questions.query: Does a PUT using an existing key in a versioning-enabled bucket overwrite the older stored version?
questions.reference_answer: No. The older version remains, and S3 assigns a new version ID and adds the newer version.

questions.query: What storage size and storage class does the selected guide attribute to a delete marker?
questions.reference_answer: Its storage size equals the UTF-8 size of its key name, described as one to four bytes per character. Delete markers use the S3 Standard storage class.

questions.query: Does permanently deleting a specified data version insert a new delete marker?
questions.reference_answer: No. When DELETE specifies the versionId, that version is permanently deleted and S3 does not insert a delete marker.

questions.query: Which IAM action does the selected ListObjectVersions opening require, despite its different API operation name?
questions.reference_answer: s3:ListBucketVersions.

questions.query: What object identifier must a GetObject request specify according to the selected API opening?
questions.reference_answer: The full object key name.

questions.query: What default access state does the selected access-control overview assign to S3 resources, and who controls additional access?
questions.reference_answer: Resources are private by default. The resource owner's account root user and appropriately permitted IAM users can access their created resources; the owner decides who else can access them and perform which actions.

questions.query: How many keys can one DeleteObjects request contain, and how is each key's outcome reported?
questions.reference_answer: Up to 1,000 keys. S3 returns success or failure per key; an object not found is reported as deleted.

questions.query: What lifecycle rule metadata determines whether its configured actions are performed?
questions.reference_answer: The rule includes an ID and enabled/disabled status. S3 performs none of the rule's actions while it is disabled.

questions.query: Does PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration patch an existing configuration or replace it?
questions.reference_answer: It creates a new configuration or replaces the existing one. Include every detail that should be retained in the new configuration.

questions.query: Which special error and HTTP status does GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration return when no lifecycle configuration exists?
questions.reference_answer: NoSuchLifecycleConfiguration with HTTP 404 Not Found.

questions.query: A 200 GB file exceeds the console limit described in this snapshot. Which interfaces and upload approach does the selected overview point me toward?
questions.reference_answer: Use the AWS CLI, an SDK, or the REST API rather than the console. The overview provides multipart upload for objects larger than the single-PUT ceiling.

questions.query: My multipart uploader keeps object metadata only in its local configuration. At what phase must it send that metadata so S3 can attach it to the final object?
questions.reference_answer: Supply the object metadata in the multipart initiation request, rather than relying on local metadata or individual part data.

questions.query: A multipart upload using additional checksums has gaps in its part numbers and completion returns HTTP 500. What documented numbering rule should I check?
questions.reference_answer: Additional-checksum multipart uploads require consecutive part numbers. The selected passage explicitly associates nonconsecutive completion with HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.

questions.query: After aborting a multipart upload, can I resume UploadPart requests using that same upload ID?
questions.reference_answer: No. The selected AbortMultipartUpload description says no additional parts can be uploaded using an aborted upload's ID.

questions.query: Several part uploads are still in progress, but ListParts does not show them. Does the selected listing guide say unfinished parts belong in that response?
questions.reference_answer: No. Returned part listings omit parts that have not finished uploading.

questions.query: CompleteMultipartUpload sends a 200 header and then whitespace for a while. Do the initial header and whitespace establish a final successful completion?
questions.reference_answer: No. Processing can take several minutes and whitespace keeps the connection from timing out. The final response can still contain an embedded error, so parse and handle its contents.

questions.query: My HEAD client receives a generic error code but no detailed exception body. Can it recover the exact server exception from that HeadObject response?
questions.reference_answer: No. HEAD has no response body and the selected description says its generic error codes do not expose the exact exception.

questions.query: A HeadObject client is assembling 9 KB of request headers. Which limit in the selected API description does this exceed?
questions.reference_answer: The documented request-header limit is 8 KB.

questions.query: BlockPublicAcls is enabled and my PUT Object includes a public ACL. Is S3 documented to accept the write and merely ignore that ACL?
questions.reference_answer: No. That setting rejects the specified PUT when it includes a public ACL. IgnorePublicAcls is the separately described ignore-without-rejecting mechanism.

questions.query: I previously used Block Public Access to suppress an existing public ACL. Could removing that block make the resource public again even if I never create another ACL?
questions.reference_answer: Yes. The selected passage says the settings do not alter existing policies or ACLs, so removing the block can expose a resource whose public policy or ACL remains.

questions.query: An account-level Block Public Access change has not appeared in every Region simultaneously. Does the selected guide promise immediate global convergence?
questions.reference_answer: No. It explicitly allows delayed or nonsimultaneous propagation, although the account settings eventually apply across all Regions.

questions.query: I enabled versioning, but an older object still has a null version ID. Does the selected version-ID passage treat that as a failed enablement?
questions.reference_answer: No. Existing objects retain their null IDs, contents and permissions; subsequently added objects receive version IDs.

questions.query: What version-count condition does the selected guide say might accompany a significant increase in 503 responses for PUT or DELETE in a versioning-enabled bucket?
questions.reference_answer: One possible condition is one or more objects with millions of versions. The passage does not establish that as the cause of every 503.

questions.query: Replication status is Pending and expiration is not acting on a current or noncurrent version. What exception is documented in the selected expiration passage?
questions.reference_answer: The selected expiration note says S3 takes no action on current or noncurrent versions whose replication status is Pending.

questions.query: My noncurrent-expiration rule specifies how many newer noncurrent versions to retain but omits Filter, and I get InvalidRequest. What requirement does the selected guide identify?
questions.reference_answer: Specifying the maximum number of noncurrent versions to retain also requires a Filter element; without it S3 generates InvalidRequest.

questions.query: Noncurrent versions with an S3 Object Lock configuration remain despite an expiration rule. What exception does the selected expiration note describe?
questions.reference_answer: The note says S3 does not take action on noncurrent versions with the S3 Object Lock configuration applied.

questions.query: An object is eligible for permanent deletion and a lifecycle transition on the same day. Which action has precedence in the selected conflict rules?
questions.reference_answer: Permanent deletion takes precedence over transition.

questions.query: A management script sends only a newly added lifecycle rule through PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration and the old rules disappear. Why is that consistent with the selected API description?
questions.reference_answer: The operation replaces the configuration rather than patching it. Retain existing details by including them in the submitted configuration.

questions.query: GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration returns NoSuchLifecycleConfiguration with 404. What is missing according to that operation's special-error description?
questions.reference_answer: The lifecycle configuration does not exist. The named error is about that configuration, not proof that the bucket itself is absent.

questions.query: Which multipart operation sends new part data in the request, and which uses an existing S3 object as the part's data source?
questions.reference_answer: UploadPart sends new data. UploadPartCopy uses an existing S3 object as the data source for the part.

questions.query: How does HeadObject differ from GET when an application only wants an object's metadata?
questions.reference_answer: HEAD retrieves the metadata without the object itself. It has the same options and response as GET except that HEAD has no response body.

questions.query: What does listing parts of a multipart upload show, compared with listing in-progress multipart uploads?
questions.reference_answer: List-parts reports finished parts for one upload. Listing multipart uploads reports uploads initiated but not yet completed or stopped; the selected guide limits each request to at most 1,000 uploads.

questions.query: How do BlockPublicAcls and IgnorePublicAcls differ for a PUT carrying a public ACL, and does either erase existing ACL records?
questions.reference_answer: BlockPublicAcls rejects the specified PUTs with public ACLs; IgnorePublicAcls permits public ACLs to be set but ignores their public grants. Neither setting rewrites or deletes the existing ACL records.

questions.query: For a bucket, how does BlockPublicPolicy differ from RestrictPublicBuckets when a public policy is involved?
questions.reference_answer: BlockPublicPolicy rejects a PUT Bucket policy that allows public access. RestrictPublicBuckets restricts access under a public policy to AWS service principals and authorized users in the owning account, blocking other cross-account access except AWS service principals. Enabling these settings does not itself rewrite the stored policy.

questions.query: What is the difference between a lifecycle transition action and an expiration action?
questions.reference_answer: A transition changes the object's storage class at the specified stage of its life. Expiration defines when an object expires and S3 deletes expired objects according to the applicable versioning behavior.

questions.query: How do Enabled and Suspended differ for objects added after setting a bucket's versioning state?
questions.reference_answer: With Enabled, added objects receive unique version IDs. With Suspended, added objects receive the version ID null.

questions.query: In a versioning-enabled bucket, how does deleting by key alone differ from deleting a specified data version by key and version ID?
questions.reference_answer: A key-only delete creates a current delete marker and returns its version ID. A delete specifying a data version removes that specific version.

questions.query: How do ordinary multipart numbering and numbering with additional checksums differ with respect to gaps?
questions.reference_answer: Ordinary multipart part numbers need not be consecutive. With additional checksums they must be consecutive; the selected passage associates nonconsecutive completion with HTTP 500.

questions.query: How does storage for a retained object version differ from storage for its delete marker?
questions.reference_answer: Each object version stores the entire object rather than a diff. A delete marker has no object data or ACL, and its storage size is the UTF-8 size of its key name in S3 Standard.

questions.query: Why might a client choose DeleteObjects instead of individual DeleteObject requests, and what is the documented batch limit?
questions.reference_answer: DeleteObjects deletes multiple named keys in one HTTP request, reducing per-request overhead. One request can contain up to 1,000 keys and reports each key's result.

questions.query: How do GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration and PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration differ in purpose and required IAM action?
questions.reference_answer: Get reads the configured lifecycle information and requires s3:GetLifecycleConfiguration. Put creates or replaces the configuration and requires s3:PutLifecycleConfiguration.

questions.query: For a multipart uploader, which operation returns the shared upload identifier, what must be retained after each part, and how does completion order the parts?
questions.reference_answer: CreateMultipartUpload returns the upload ID. Retain each part number and its returned ETag for completion. CompleteMultipartUpload assembles the supplied parts in ascending part-number order.

questions.query: Will an abandoned multipart upload expire automatically by default, and what lifecycle mechanism can clean up its parts after a chosen number of days?
questions.reference_answer: The overview says initiated uploads have no expiry and require explicit completion or stopping. A lifecycle AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload action can stop incomplete uploads after a specified number of days since initiation and delete their parts.

questions.query: I maintain an already-uploaded object and a separate ongoing multipart upload. How can I add a checksum algorithm to the former, and inspect part checksums on the latter?
questions.reference_answer: Copy the existing object and choose the checksum algorithm while copying. For multipart uploads still in progress, use ListParts to retrieve the part checksum values.

questions.query: According to the selected guide, what must happen before downloading bytes 0–500 from an archived object, and what range form does its CLI example use?
questions.reference_answer: Restore the archived object first. The range example uses the bytes= prefix, specifically --range bytes=0-500, with an output file.

questions.query: I need selected bytes from an object owned by someone else. What access route does the download guide suggest, and can one GET request fetch two disjoint ranges?
questions.reference_answer: Ask the owner for a presigned URL allowing the download. S3 does not support retrieving multiple ranges of data in a single GET request.

questions.query: A client checks metadata before fetching an object's contents. Which operation avoids the object body, and what key information does the subsequent GetObject request need?
questions.reference_answer: Use HeadObject for metadata without the object body. GetObject must specify the full key name.

questions.query: How can an authorized client read a noncurrent data version and then permanently delete that version when the bucket has MFA Delete enabled?
questions.reference_answer: Specify the version ID when reading the noncurrent version. For permanent deletion use DeleteObject with versionId; with MFA Delete enabled, include x-amz-mfa and use HTTPS.

questions.query: When enabling versioning on a bucket that already has objects and an expiration policy, what happens to those existing objects and what policy addition preserves permanent deletion of old versions?
questions.reference_answer: Existing objects retain their null version IDs, data and permissions. Add a noncurrent expiration policy if the previous permanent-delete behavior must continue after versioning is enabled.

questions.query: Why can an existing lifecycle rule still delete objects despite a deny-all bucket policy, and which permission controls replacing the lifecycle configuration?
questions.reference_answer: The selected guide says a bucket policy cannot prevent lifecycle deletions or transitions. The API requires s3:PutLifecycleConfiguration to create or replace the configuration; an explicit deny still supersedes permission grants.

questions.query: What makes a lone delete marker expired for lifecycle cleanup, and does leaving that marker consume the old object's full data size?
questions.reference_answer: It is expired when all object versions have been deleted and only a single marker remains; lifecycle can remove it. A marker has no object data and its storage size is its key's UTF-8 size, not the old object's full size.

questions.query: Can a direct PutObject update only one metadata field, and when must a multipart uploader provide metadata for its final object?
questions.reference_answer: PutObject must send the entire object with updated metadata rather than changing only one field. Multipart object metadata must be provided at initiation.

questions.query: An object's current version is a delete marker, but I want a byte range from an older data version. How can I select the data version, and may I request multiple disjoint ranges in one GET?
questions.reference_answer: Select the noncurrent data version by its version ID. The selected range guide does not support multiple ranges in a single GET.

questions.query: A diagnostic client lists versions and checks a missing key with HEAD. Which separate permissions affect listing versions and HEAD's 403-versus-404 distinction?
questions.reference_answer: ListObjectVersions requires s3:ListBucketVersions. HEAD requires the relevant s3:GetObject permission; for a missing object, s3:ListBucket determines whether the selected description returns 404 instead of 403.

questions.query: I have 1,001 specific object versions to delete. What batch limit constrains DeleteObjects, and should my client invent or edit their version IDs?
questions.reference_answer: A DeleteObjects request accepts at most 1,000 keys, with optional version IDs, so 1,001 items require at least two such requests. Use S3-generated opaque version IDs; clients cannot choose or edit them.

questions.query: How can a management client read existing lifecycle rules and replace them without accidentally dropping retained rules, and which two IAM actions are needed?
questions.reference_answer: Read with GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration using s3:GetLifecycleConfiguration. When writing with PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration, include the details to retain because it replaces the configuration; that write requires s3:PutLifecycleConfiguration.

questions.query: Which rule status prevents lifecycle actions from running, and what extra requirement applies when NoncurrentVersionExpiration specifies a count of versions to retain?
questions.reference_answer: A disabled rule performs no actions. Specifying the maximum number of noncurrent versions also requires a Filter element, or S3 returns InvalidRequest.

questions.query: What default encryption does the selected upload overview describe, and which KMS actions and policy grants are needed for a separate cross-account SSE-KMS multipart upload?
questions.reference_answer: The overview describes SSE-S3 as the default. The multipart permissions passage requires kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt for the relevant operations; when the IAM principal is in a different account from the KMS key, permissions are needed in both the key policy and the IAM user or role policy.

questions.query: After aborting a multipart upload, which API check confirms all parts are gone, and what IAM action is required to make that check?
questions.reference_answer: Call ListParts and verify an empty parts list. The multipart permissions table requires s3:ListMultipartUploadParts for listing parts.

questions.query: How do IgnorePublicAcls and Bucket owner enforced Object Ownership each affect ACL-based access, and does the former erase stored ACLs?
questions.reference_answer: IgnorePublicAcls ignores public ACL grants without removing their stored ACLs. Bucket owner enforced disables ACLs, makes the bucket owner own the objects, and manages access exclusively through policies.
